description: Verify that DUT replies to an ICMP Echo Request that arrives carrying TTL=0 — the host receive path MUST NOT discard packets based on TTL value, even when zero (RFC 1122 §3.2.1.7: 'a host MUST NOT send a datagram with TTL = 0; however, it MUST NOT silently discard a received datagram solely on the basis of its TTL value')
approach:
[Objective]
TTL is a routing-time concept; once a packet has been delivered to its destination, its remaining TTL is irrelevant. RFC 1122 explicitly forbids hosts from silently dropping a received datagram solely because of low TTL, even TTL=0. DUT must reply normally.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request with IPv4 TTL=0

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: Echo Reply

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an Echo Reply.

[Fail condition]
Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit a Reply, presumably because it dropped the Request based on TTL=0. RFC 1122 violation.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied to TTL=0 Request — receive path correctly ignores TTL
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not reply to TTL=0 Request — likely dropped on TTL (RFC 1122 violation)
